53031-the-barton-experiment.title: The Barton Experiment
53031-the-barton-experiment.creator: Unknown
53031-the-barton-experiment.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Long and loud rang all the church bells of Barton on a certain summer evening twenty years ago. It was not a Sunday evening, for during an accidental lull there was heard, afar off yet distinctly, the unsanctified notes of the mail-carrier’s horn.

arxiv-1706-05530.title: Holographic Van der Waals phase transition of the higher dimensional electrically charged hairy black hole Journal: Eur. Phys. J. C
arxiv-1706-05530.creator: Hui-Ling Li addr1,e1, Zhong-Wen Feng addr2
arxiv-1706-05530.description: Abstract With motivation by holography, employing black hole entropy, two point connection function and entanglement entropy, we show that, for the higher dimensional Anti-de Sitter charged hairy black hole in the fixed charged ensemble, a Van der Waals-like phase transition can be observed.

arxiv-2104-09896.title: Boundary Condition Independence of Non-Hermitian Hamiltonian Dynamics
arxiv-2104-09896.creator: Liang Mao, Tianshu Deng, Pengfei Zhang
arxiv-2104-09896.description: Abstract Non-Hermitian skin effect, namely that the eigenvalues and eigenstates of a non-Hermitian tight-binding Hamiltonian have significant differences under open or periodic boundary conditions, is a remarkable phenomenon of non-Hermitian systems. Inspired by the presence of the non-Hermitian skin effect, we study the evolution of wave-packets in non-Hermitian systems, which can be determined using the single-particle Green’s function.

arxiv-2104-11989.title: Lie symmetries of a third order PDE system
arxiv-2104-11989.creator: Reza Dastranj
arxiv-2104-11989.description: Abstract . In this paper we show that a third order PDE system that is a general form of a CR-geometry PDE system has at most a ten-dimensional Lie symmetry algebra. We also show that this estimate is precise. August 9, 2026 1.

arxiv-2111-14540.title: Dynamical low-rank approximations of solutions to the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation
arxiv-2111-14540.creator: Martin Eigel, Reinhold Schneider, David Sommer
arxiv-2111-14540.description: Abstract We present a novel method to approximate optimal feedback laws for nonlinear optimal control based on low-rank tensor train (TT) decompositions. The approach is based on the Dirac-Frenkel variational principle with the modification that the optimisation uses an empirical risk. Compared to current state-of-the-art TT methods, our approach exhibits a greatly reduced computational burden while achieving comparable results.

arxiv-2210-13082.title: Are Deep Sequence Classifiers Good at Non-Trivial Generalization?
arxiv-2210-13082.creator: Francesco Cazzaro, Ariadna Quattoni, Xavier Carreras
arxiv-2210-13082.description: Abstract Recent advances in deep learning models for sequence classification have greatly improved their classification accuracy, specially when large training sets are available. However, several works have suggested that under some settings the predictions made by these models are poorly calibrated.

arxiv-2301-07981.title: Continuously Reliable Detection of New-Normal Misinformation: Semantic Masking and Contrastive Smoothing in High-Density Latent Regions
arxiv-2301-07981.creator: Abhijit Suprem, Joao Eduardo Ferreira, Calton Pu
arxiv-2301-07981.description: Abstract Toxic misinformation campaigns have caused significant societal harm, e . g ., affecting elections and COVID-19 information awareness. Unfortunately, despite successes of (gold standard) retrospective studies of misinformation that confirmed their harmful effects after the fact, they arrive too late for timely intervention and reduction of such harm.

arxiv-2306-01768.title: A Quantitative Review on Language Model Efficiency Research
arxiv-2306-01768.creator: Meng Jiang, Hy Dang, Lingbo Tong
arxiv-2306-01768.description: Abstract Language models (LMs) are being scaled and becoming powerful. Improving their efficiency is one of the core research topics in neural information processing systems. Tay et al. 2022a provided a comprehensive overview of efficient Transformers that have become an indispensable staple in the field of NLP.

arxiv-2401-02530.title: Diffusion-driven deposition model suggests stiffer gels deposit more efficiently in microchannel flows
arxiv-2401-02530.creator: Barrett T. Smith, Sara M. Hashmi
arxiv-2401-02530.description: Abstract The behavior of crosslinking polymer solutions as they transition from liquid-like to solid-like material in flow determines success or failure in several applications. Dilute polymer solutions flow easily, while concentrated polymers or crosslinked polymer gels can clog pores, nozzles, or channels.

arxiv-2405-11677.title: Advancing 6-DoF Instrument Pose Estimation in Variable X-Ray Imaging Geometries PubID: pubid: Author Version - 10.1109/TIP.2024.3378469 © 2024 IEEE
arxiv-2405-11677.creator: Christiaan G.A. Viviers, Lena Filatova, Maurice Termeer, Peter H.N. de With, Fons van der Sommen
arxiv-2405-11677.description: Abstract Accurate 6-DoF pose estimation of surgical instruments during minimally invasive surgeries can substantially improve treatment strategies and eventual surgical outcome. Existing deep learning methods have achieved accurate results, but they require custom approaches for each object and laborious setup and training environments often stretching to extensive simulations, whilst lacking real-time computation.

arxiv-2509-07239.title: Safe Gap-based Planning in Dynamic Settings
arxiv-2509-07239.creator: Max Asselmeier, Abdel Zaro, Dhruv Ahuja, Ye Zhao, and Patricio A. Vela
arxiv-2509-07239.description: Abstract This chapter extends the family of perception-informed gap-based local planners to dynamic environments. Existing perception-informed local planners that operate in dynamic environments often rely on emergent or empirical robustness for collision avoidance as opposed to performing formal analysis of dynamic obstacles. This proposed planner, dynamic gap , explicitly addresses dynamic obstacles through several steps in the planning pipeline.

pmc-10736379.title: MATCHING DYADIC RESEARCH QUESTIONS WITH DYADIC ANALYTIC MODELS
pmc-10736379.creator: Joshua Novak
pmc-10736379.description: Examining shared and common experiences between dyads affords opportunities to answer interesting research questions using dyadic data. Emerging dyadic methodology has expanded the types of research questions researchers can ask and answer. This session aims to equip researchers with knowledge and resources for grant writing, when planning new data collection projects, or when conducting secondary data analyses.

pmc-11352189.title: Corazonin Stimulates Ecdysteroid Synthesis during the Molting Process of the Swimming Crab, Portunus trituberculatus
pmc-11352189.creator: Xi Xie, Jun Zhang, Shisheng Tu, Qi Zhou, Dongfa Zhu, Lutz Auerswald, Xianliang Meng, Yafei Duan
pmc-11352189.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple SummaryFunctional studies of neuropeptides are of great significance in revealing the neuroendocrine regulation mechanism in crustaceans, and in guiding and developing artificial regulation techniques in economic species. In this paper, we investigated the effect of a crustacean neuropeptide corazonin (Crz) on ecdysteroid synthesis based on the high expression of Crz receptor in the Y-organ, the main site of ecdysteroid synthesis.

pmc-11492456.title: Elaeagnus angustifolia L. fruit alleviates diarrhea via regulating intestinal microbiota and short chain fatty acids
pmc-11492456.creator: Xiatiguli Abulizi, Ming-hui Shi, Yue-mei Jia, Lei Xu, Lei-ling Shi, Lan Pan
pmc-11492456.description: Fruits of Elaeagnus angustifolia L. have been used as Uyghur medicine due to the properties of treating spleen and stomach weakness, indigestion, enteritis, diarrhea, lung heat, and cough. However, the anti-diarrhea mechanism was still not clear. This study explored the mechanism of E. angustifolia fruit alleviated diarrhea from the perspective of gut microbiota.

pmc-12511321.title: Terahertz time domain spectroscopy technique used for evaluation of thickness and optical cum dielectric properties of table and fertile eggshells
pmc-12511321.creator: Juveria Iram, Naveen Periketi, Aleem Basha, A K Chaudhary, Kaleem Ahmed Jaleeli, R Purshotham
pmc-12511321.description: The paper reports the use of THz time domain spectroscopy for the measurements of thickness, refractive index and dielectric constants of chicken egg shells. Twelve numbers of table and fertile egg samples were selected. The experiment was performed in the reflection geometry using a fiber-coupled terahertz source between 0 and 4.0 THz range.

pmc-12927250.title: Retrospective study of 115 patients with diabetes mellitus complicated by retrograde ejaculation
pmc-12927250.creator: Chuangui Li, Huan Wang, Siqi Li, Tianzi Zhang, Hao Li, Chongbo Wang
pmc-12927250.description: BackgroundRetrograde ejaculation is a significant complication of diabetes mellitus, yet its association with other sexual dysfunctions remains under-characterized. Current literature often treats it as an isolated fertility issue, overlooking potential co-morbidities. This study aimed to comprehensively profile the clinical characteristics of diabetic men with retrograde ejaculation and investigate the independent risk factors for severe sexual dysfunction, specifically moderate-to-severe erectile dysfunction.

pmc-13550073.title: Low-level laser irradiation stimulated tumoricidal impacts and dose-dependent modulation of Wnt signaling in three-dimensional human colorectal cancer microspheres
pmc-13550073.creator: Hesam Saghaei Bagheri, Cigir Biray Avci, Nafiseh Didar Khosrowshahi, Fereshteh Vaziri Nezamdoust, Somayyeh Rashidi, Ali Baradar Khoshfetrat, Habib Tajalli, Reza Rahbarghazi, Asghar Khalilnezhad, Elham Shahriyari, Fereshteh Valipour
pmc-13550073.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The high incidence of colorectal cancer (CRC) has been a big challenge in human medicine. Along with several available therapies, specific modalities, e.g., low-level laser irradiation (LLLI), have been introduced to achieve proper regenerative outcomes. Unfortunately, most studies have investigated the tumoricidal effects of LLLI on cancer cells using a 2D culture system with less comparable capacity to in vivo conditions. Here, the detrimental impacts of LLLI were studied in human CRC cells encapsulated inside alginate-gelatin (Alg-Gel) microspheres after 48 h.

pmc-13585268.title: Accelerometer-derived real-world sleep stages and risk of incident diseases: A UK Biobank cohort study and phenome-wide association analysis
pmc-13585268.creator: Jingsong Luo, Ruiyi Liu, Jie Yin, Wangnan Cao, Shengzhi Sun, Rui Chen
pmc-13585268.description: BackgroundPrevious studies utilizing self-reported data or polysomnography have found that poor sleep quality is associated with increased risk of morbidity and mortality. However, the association between real-world sleep patterns, including sleep stages, duration, and fragmentation, measured objectively with physiological data and the risk of incident disease among middle-aged and older adults has not yet been systematically evaluated.
